newsitem.title: UK: TABLE TENNIS-WALDNER ON A HIGH.
newsitem.headline: TABLE TENNIS-WALDNER ON A HIGH.

text.p: Swedish world number two Jan-Ove Waldner seems to have found the secret of conquering the years as he reaches the table tennis twilight zone.
The 31-year-old European champion is even better now than when he won the Olympic gold medal at Barcelona in 1992, he said on Monday night after reaching his fourth world championship final.
Waldner, champion in 1989 and runner-up in 1987 and 1991, had just swept aside China's Yan Sen to record his sixth successive straight-sets victory.
"I have never done that in a major tournament before, although I lost only one set in the Barcelona Olympics," Waldner said.
"I am playing very well now. I am a better player now than I was at the Olympics in Barcelona. The game is getting better every year. The game is quicker but I can still cope.
Waldner was not worried about facing Vladimir Samsonov, who beat him 21-6 21-7 in the team event.
"I have more experience but his is young and very hungry to win this title," he said of his 21-year-old opponent from Belarus.

Asked how long he could carry on at such a high level, Waldner replied jokingly: "I hope until tomorrow. When I think I cannot win the big tournaments maybe I will stop. But it could be one year or four years. You never know, maybe one more Olympics will be possible."
Swedish team manager Ulf Carlsson was convinced Waldner was still a world beater as his record showed.

"The game is developing every year and he is getting older every year. The conclusion from that is he is better than ever. Normally it should be harder now than to win four or five years ago but he can compete at this level, especially for the last two or three days, it is amazing."
Carlsson said Waldner was a man for the big occasion.

"Jan-Ove is a player who has always tried to find new things to develop his game and also he is very good in preparing for big tournaments. In the season sometimes he is a little up and down but never for big tournaements. The sign of a very good player is that he always plays very good at the biggest tournaments."
